etymologies.heading: Etymology 1
paragraphs: From Latin dilapidō (“to scatter, consume, throw away”) +‎ -ate (verb-forming suffix), from dis- (“asunder”) +‎ lapidō (“to stone”), from lapis (“stone”). Compare French dilapider.
senses: (transitive) To cause to become ruined or put into disrepair.

etymologies.heading: Etymology 2
paragraphs: Learned borrowing from Latin dīlapidātus, perfect passive participle of dilapidō (“squander, consume, throw away”), see Etymology 1 and -ate (adjective-forming suffix) for more.
